rv.q: Tata’s staging takes many counterintuitive tacks here, several of them orthogonal to the play itself.
But the lack of compelling performances renders this complex tragedy, and its conflicted central character, frustratingly flat and stubbornly unengaging.
You don't need gimmicks when your cast is this good.

Now Ash K. Tata takes it on for Theatre for a New Audience at the Polonsky Shakespeare Center, in a bewildering production that had a not-insignificant number of theatergoers leaving at intermission at the preview I attended.
